findings.element: Notes → the peel/send crossing: .peelBoundary, the peel and send live regions, .peelWhy, and the open-task announcement
findings.problem: Driving one crossing (lift a note, select words, peel, send, open in Tasks) makes the surface promise the note is safe FIVE times, in five wordings and three tenses: .peelBoundary "Your note stays here. Tasks only ever receives the exact words you pick and check below."; on peel, aloud, "Tasks receives these words and nothing else from this note. The rest of what you wrote stays private here."; .peelWhy "Your note is still here, still private, still yours to edit."; on send, aloud, "Sent to Tasks. Your note stayed here. In The house."; on arrival, aloud, "Opened in Tasks. Your note stayed in Notes." The file states the rule itself elsewhere — "One guarantee, one carrier" (master.html, discard-speech) — and the overdue filter keeps it exactly (one string, printed and announced). Two costs. Register: "still here, still private, still yours to edit" is the only string in the suite that reaches for rhetoric, and a product that repeats a promise five times sounds like one that expects not to be believed. Information: the card lands in To do and NOTHING says so — not the receipt, not either announcement, not at 1440 or 390. What she IS told is "In The house", the destination she chose herself on the picker one keystroke earlier. The copy hands back what she typed and withholds what the system decided, at the one moment that is the entire argument for a suite existing.
findings.fix: Say the guarantee once, where it is load-bearing, and spend the rest on the lane. Keep .peelBoundary verbatim as the single statement. (1) Peel live region: drop the two guarantee sentences, announce only "The words you picked: <words>." (2) .peelWhy: replace "Your note is still here, still private, still yours to edit." with "In To do. Your note is still here." (3) Send live region: replace with "Sent to Tasks. In To do, <destination>." (4) Open-task live region: replace with "Opened in Tasks. <task title>, in To do." Lane name read from the tray the card landed in, through the same accessor the tray head uses, so it can never drift.

findings.element: The spine's More tile (.railTile aria-label "More") and its live region — master.html:11443
findings.problem: Press More: .morePop opens, aria-expanded flips to "true", Home / Inbox / Help / Settings appear each marked "Not here yet" — and the live region announces "More, closed." Press again: the menu closes, aria-expanded is "false", and it announces "More, open." The announcement is the exact reverse of what happened, in both directions, on pointer and on Enter, in all three products (reproduced in notes.notebook, tasks.board and timeline.desk). Cause: say(moreOpen ? "More, open." : "More, closed.") is called OUTSIDE the morph callback, so it reads moreOpen before the callback flips it. The sibling control does it correctly — Projects (master.html:14990) calls say() inside the callback, after projOpen = !projOpen, and announces the truth. The brief calls the closed doors a designed answer rather than a gap; this is the door whose own state announcement is false, which spends exactly the honesty the doors were kept to buy.
findings.fix: master.html:11443 — capture the state before the toggle and announce from it: replace say(moreOpen ? "More, open." : "More, closed.") with say(wasOpen ? "More, closed." : "More, open.") (wasOpen is already in scope two lines above at 11431). Add an assertion to interaction-check.mjs that presses More, reads aria-expanded and the live region in the same pass, and fails if they disagree — then the same for Projects, Settings, Planning and the subtasks disclosure.

findings.element: Notes head, [data-act="privacy"] — the "Private to you" button; string at master.html:19716
findings.problem: Every other closed door paints a visible answer beside itself: press Notes options, Read a photo or the account tile and an "Not here yet" card appears (measured at 80, 250, 700 and 1600ms). Press "Private to you" and nothing is ever painted, at any of those times — it answers only in the live region. It is an enabled, focusable, in-tab-order button that does nothing a sighted person can see. The mechanism is why: the suite paints a door's answer only when the control carries aria-disabled="true" and a title matching /Not here yet/ (master.html:19457), and this button has neither, so it falls through to the ELSEWHERE table. And the sentence it does say breaks the doors' own ratified grammar — "name the thing, then Not here yet., then at most one sentence of reassurance": it reads "Yours until you send something on. Your privacy settings. Not here yet." The name arrives second, and the first sentence is a verbatim repeat of the second half of the button's own accessible name, which the reader heard one keystroke earlier.
findings.fix: Put it through the same path as the other three doors. On the "Private to you" button set aria-disabled="true" and title="Your privacy settings. Not here yet.", and delete the privacy entry from the ELSEWHERE table at master.html:19716. It then paints the visible card like Notes options and the account tile, and speaks in the doors' one grammar. Leave the button's accessible name as it is — "Private to you. Yours until you send something on." is the status, and the title is now the door.

findings.element: Timeline at ≤720: .b-act.b-more (the head's "···") and the dock's .railTile More
findings.problem: At 390 in timeline.owner-flight two buttons are on screen at once whose accessible name is exactly "More", both aria-haspopup="menu", 643px apart (y=140 and y=783). They open unrelated places: the head's opens a menu — itself also labelled "More" — holding Preview and Get the link, i.e. this plan's sharing; the dock's opens "Also in Signal Studio: Home, Inbox, Help, Settings", i.e. the rest of the suite. A screen-reader user hears "More, menu" twice on one screen and cannot tell which is which; a sighted user meets "···" with no word at all. The collision exists only at ≤720, where the head collapses Add a moment / Preview / Get the link into the dots — at 1440 they are spelled out and there is one "More" on screen, which is why no frame shows it.
findings.fix: Name the head's control for what it opens, not for the glyph. Set aria-label="Share this plan" on .b-act.b-more and the same aria-label on the .b-menu it opens (it currently carries aria-label="More"). Leave the dock tile as "More". Add an assertion to interaction-check.mjs that, at each configured viewport and state, collects the accessible names of all visible controls with aria-haspopup and fails on any duplicate.

findings.element: The dictation floor's disclosure, N.copy.voiceDisclosure — master.html:9410, rendered only at 18684
findings.problem: The one privacy claim on the ink floor reads "Signal Studio keeps the words, not the audio. Typing stays on this device until you save." It renders on exactly one screen in the product, and it is the screen where nobody types. The first sentence tells her Signal Studio keeps the words — so the words go somewhere. The second sentence, which is the one that has to answer the question she is actually asking while she is mid-sentence with the microphone open — does what I just said leave this device before I save? — is about a different verb, and reads as if it were lifted from the capture field. Two sentences, and the load-bearing one answers the wrong question on the most sensitive surface in the suite.
findings.fix: master.html:9410 — change the second sentence to name the act the screen is performing: "Signal Studio keeps the words, not the audio. What you say stays on this device until you save." Same length, same two-sentence shape, same register, and it now answers the question the floor raises.

biggestWin: The register holds, and so does the arithmetic. Across three products and ten states there is not one exclamation mark, not one marketing sentence, not one piece of jargon, and not one Title Case label — plain declarative English in sentence case throughout, with one grammar for a date, one for a count, and closed doors that say plainly they are not built instead of pretending. And it survives driving, which is where copy usually breaks: "8 to decide" reconciles against five separate group tails, "14 notes" against fourteen rows, "5 of 13 done / 38%" becomes "5 of 14 / 36%" and "7 to decide" the instant a note crosses the seam, and the dense fold reports exactly the number of cards outside the scroller in every lane at 1920, 1440 and 1280. The five lane notes — "Agreed and ready to start.", "In motion right now.", "Being checked before it goes out.", "Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision.", "Finished and put away." — teach the whole board in five lines with no tooltip anywhere. And the filter is a model of the rule the rest of the product should follow: "Showing 1 overdue task. 12 others are hidden." is one string in one grammar, printed on screen and announced aloud, released by "Showing all work." That is copy someone lived with, not copy someone wrote.
